events.title: Austronesian Migration
events.description: Austronesian-speaking peoples migrated from Taiwan to the Philippine islands, bringing agricultural technology and language. Most modern Filipino ethnic groups belong to the Austronesian language family, closely related to Taiwan's indigenous peoples.

events.title: Early Trade Networks
events.description: The Philippine islands began trading with China, Southeast Asia, and India. Archaeological findings show extensive commercial contact between early Philippines and the outside world.

events.title: Early Political Entities Form
events.description: Multiple 'barangays' (village communities) emerged across the Philippines, small political entities ruled by chieftains (datus) that became the foundation of Philippine political organization.

events.title: Flourishing Trade with China
events.description: During the Song and Yuan periods, Philippines traded frequently with China. Large quantities of Chinese goods flowed into the Philippines, with abundant Chinese ceramics excavated.

events.title: Islam Enters Philippines
events.description: Islam spread to southern Philippines (Mindanao and Sulu) through Arab and Malay traders. Islamic states like the Sultanate of Sulu were established.

events.title: Sultanate of Sulu Founded
events.description: Abu Bakr established the Sultanate of Sulu, one of the Philippines' earliest Islamic states. The Sultanate controlled the Sulu Archipelago and parts of Mindanao.

events.title: Sultanate of Maguindanao Founded
events.description: The Sultanate of Maguindanao, established in Mindanao, became the most powerful Islamic state in southern Philippines, controlling vast territory.

events.title: Magellan Arrives in the Philippines
events.description: Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan (exploring for Spain) reached the Philippine islands, landing in Cebu. This was the first European contact with the Philippines.

events.title: Magellan's Death
events.description: Magellan intervened in local tribal conflicts and was killed in battle on Mactan Island by warriors led by Chief Lapu-Lapu. Lapu-Lapu became the Philippines' first hero of resistance against foreign invasion.

events.title: Spanish Colonization Begins
events.description: Miguel López de Legazpi led a Spanish expedition to the Philippines, establishing the first Spanish colonial foothold in Cebu. The Philippines began 333 years of Spanish rule.

events.title: Manila Established as Capital
events.description: Spain conquered Manila from Rajah Sulayman's rule on Luzon, establishing it as capital of the Spanish East Indies. Manila became an important center of Pacific trade.

events.title: Limahong Besieges Manila
events.description: Chinese pirate Limahong led his fleet to besiege Spanish colonial Manila. Though the siege failed, it demonstrated Chinese maritime power's influence on the Philippines.

events.title: Manila Galleon Trade
events.description: Spain established the Manila Galleon trade route between Manila and Acapulco, Mexico, lasting 250 years. This route connected Asia and the Americas, making the Philippines an East-West trade hub.

events.title: Forced Christianization
events.description: Spanish missionaries massively spread Catholicism in the Philippines. Except for southern Muslim regions, most Filipinos converted to Catholicism, making it Asia's only predominantly Catholic nation.

events.title: Chinese Massacre
events.description: Spanish colonizers massacred about 20,000 overseas Chinese in Manila, the first of multiple anti-Chinese incidents in Philippine history. But Chinese influence in the Philippines did not disappear.

events.title: British Briefly Occupy Manila
events.description: During the Seven Years' War, Britain occupied Manila for nearly two years. Following the Treaty of Paris, Britain returned the Philippines to Spain.

events.title: Cavite Mutiny
events.description: Filipino soldiers at Cavite Fort rebelled. Spanish authorities used this as a pretext to execute three Filipino priests (Gomburza), sparking Philippine nationalist consciousness.

events.title: Noli Me Tangere Published
events.description: Philippine national hero José Rizal published the novel 'Noli Me Tangere' in Europe, exposing Spanish colonial corruption and brutality, inspiring nationalist sentiments.

events.title: Katipunan Founded
events.description: Andres Bonifacio and others founded the Katipunan secret society, committed to achieving Philippine independence through revolution. This was the beginning of the Philippine Revolution.

events.title: Philippine Revolution Breaks Out
events.description: Katipunan launched anti-Spanish uprising, beginning the Philippine Revolution. Bonifacio issued 'Cry of Pugad Lawin' calling for revolution, tearing Spanish documents, marking revolution's start.

events.title: Rizal Executed
events.description: José Rizal was executed by Spanish authorities on treason charges. His martyrdom made him the Philippines' greatest national hero, inspiring the revolution to continue.

events.title: Aguinaldo Becomes Revolutionary Leader
events.description: Emilio Aguinaldo prevailed in revolutionary internal power struggle (Bonifacio was executed), becoming revolutionary leader and president of the provisional government.

events.title: Philippine Declaration of Independence
events.description: Emilio Aguinaldo declared Philippine independence in Kawit, proclaiming the First Philippine Republic. June 12 became Philippine Independence Day. However, this independence was neither internationally recognized nor realized.

events.title: Spanish-American War and US Intervention
events.description: Spanish-American War broke out, US Navy defeated Spanish fleet at Manila Bay. Treaty of Paris ceded Philippines to US, Philippines transitioned from Spanish to American colonial rule.

events.title: Treaty of Paris
events.description: Following the Spanish-American War, Spain ceded the Philippines to the US for $20 million. Filipinos were not consulted, sparking deep resentment.

events.title: Philippine-American War
events.description: Philippine revolutionary forces resisted American occupation, sparking the Philippine-American War. The war resulted in over 200,000 Filipino deaths, with the US ultimately controlling the Philippines. Aguinaldo was captured in 1901.

events.title: US Civil Government Established
events.description: The US established civil government in the Philippines, with William Howard Taft as first Governor-General. Americans began modernizing Philippine infrastructure and education.

events.title: First Philippine Assembly
events.description: The Philippines held elections for the Philippine Assembly, the first national-level elections in Asia. This began Philippine experience with democratic institutions.

events.title: Jones Law
events.description: The US Congress passed the Jones Law, promising eventual Philippine independence and establishing a bicameral Philippine Legislature, expanding Filipino self-governance.

events.title: Commonwealth Established
events.description: The Philippine Commonwealth was established as a transitional government, with Manuel Quezon as president. The US promised full independence in 10 years.

events.title: Japanese Invasion of the Philippines
events.description: Hours after Pearl Harbor, Japan began attacking the Philippines. US and Philippine forces mounted resistance.

events.title: Japanese Occupation
events.description: Japan occupied the Philippines, establishing a puppet government. The occupation was brutal, with guerrilla forces continuing resistance. An estimated 1 million Filipinos died during the occupation.

events.title: Manila Liberation and Destruction
events.description: US forces liberated Manila but the battle caused massive destruction, with 100,000 civilian deaths. Manila was one of WWII's most devastated cities.

events.title: Philippine Independence
events.description: The US formally recognized Philippine independence, establishing the Third Philippine Republic. Manuel Roxas became the first president after independence. July 4 (later changed to June 12) became Philippine Independence Day.

events.title: Hukbalahap Rebellion
events.description: Communist Hukbalahap guerrillas continued armed struggle in central Luzon. The government eventually suppressed the rebellion through military and land reform efforts.

events.title: Post-War Reconstruction and US Relations
events.description: The Philippines rebuilt after war, remaining closely aligned with the US. Military bases and economic aid continued, making the Philippines an important US ally in Asia.

events.title: Marcos Becomes President
events.description: Ferdinand Marcos was elected president. Initially promising reform, he later became increasingly authoritarian.

events.title: Jabidah Massacre
events.description: Filipino Muslim soldiers were allegedly massacred on Corregidor Island while training for an operation against Sabah. This event sparked the Moro separatist movement.

events.title: Marcos Reelected
events.description: Marcos was reelected, becoming the first Philippine president to serve a second term. His second term saw worsening economic problems and social unrest.

events.title: Moro National Liberation Front Founded
events.description: The MNLF was established, launching armed struggle for Moro (Muslim Filipino) independence in Mindanao. This conflict became one of Asia's longest-running insurgencies.

events.title: Marcos Declares Martial Law
events.description: Ferdinand Marcos declared martial law citing national security, closing Congress, arresting opposition, and implementing dictatorial rule. Martial law lasted nearly 10 years.

events.title: New Constitution Takes Effect
events.description: The Marcos government promulgated a new constitution, changing the government system from presidential to parliamentary, effectively strengthening Marcos's power.

events.title: Tripoli Agreement
events.description: The Philippine government signed an agreement with the MNLF in Libya, promising autonomy for Mindanao's Muslim regions. But implementation was poor and conflict continued.

events.title: Martial Law Officially Lifted
events.description: Marcos lifted martial law, but authoritarian rule continued. Marcos family corruption was rampant, with economic problems worsening.

events.title: Benigno Aquino Assassinated
events.description: Opposition leader Benigno Aquino was assassinated at Manila airport upon returning from exile. This event shocked the nation and sparked massive anti-Marcos movements.

events.title: People Power Revolution (EDSA Revolution)
events.description: Following a disputed presidential election, millions of Filipinos peacefully demonstrated on EDSA Avenue against Marcos. The military defected, and Marcos was forced into exile in the US. Corazon Aquino (Benigno's widow) became president.

events.title: New Constitution Promulgated
events.description: The Aquino government promulgated a new constitution, restoring the presidential system, limiting presidential powers, and guaranteeing human rights and democracy. This constitution remains in force today.

events.title: Mount Pinatubo Eruption
events.description: Mount Pinatubo erupted, the second-largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century. Ash covered vast areas, forcing closure of Clark Air Base.

events.title: US Military Bases Withdraw
events.description: After the Philippine Senate refused to extend the lease, US forces withdrew from Subic Bay Naval Base, ending nearly a century of American military presence in the Philippines.

events.title: Peace Agreement with MNLF
events.description: The Ramos government signed a final peace agreement with the MNLF, establishing a Muslim autonomous region in Mindanao. But other armed groups continued resistance.

events.title: Asian Financial Crisis
events.description: The Asian Financial Crisis affected the Philippines, with the peso devaluing and economic growth slowing. But the Philippines was relatively less affected.

events.title: Second EDSA Revolution
events.description: President Estrada faced impeachment over corruption scandals, with mass demonstrations forcing him from power. Vice President Arroyo succeeded him.

events.title: Typhoon Haiyan
events.description: Super Typhoon Haiyan struck the Philippines, particularly Tacloban City in Leyte Province. One of the strongest tropical cyclones on record, it killed over 6,000 people.

events.title: Duterte Elected President
events.description: Davao City Mayor Rodrigo Duterte was elected president. Known for his iron-fisted approach to crime, he implemented a 'War on Drugs' policy that sparked human rights controversies.

events.title: Battle of Marawi
events.description: ISIS-affiliated militants occupied Marawi City in Mindanao, with government forces conducting a five-month siege. The battle caused massive casualties and destruction, with government forces eventually recapturing the city.

events.title: Bangsamoro Autonomous Region Established
events.description: Following a referendum, the new Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) was established, replacing the old autonomous region and granting greater autonomy to southern Muslim areas.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.description: The Philippines was severely hit by COVID-19, implementing strict lockdown measures. The pandemic devastated the economy, with unemployment rising.

events.title: Marcos Jr. Elected President
events.description: Ferdinand Marcos's son 'Bongbong' Marcos was elected president, with Sara Duterte (Duterte's daughter) as vice president. The Marcos family's return to power sparked controversy.

events.title: South China Sea Disputes Escalate
events.description: Territorial disputes between the Philippines and China in the South China Sea escalated. The Philippines strengthened its military alliance with the US, allowing American forces to use more Philippine bases.
